newsitem.title: FRANCE: French air strike compounds transport woes.
newsitem.headline: French air strike compounds transport woes.

text.p: A strike by French pilots and crews cut flights for a second day on Thursday, compounding transport woes in France on the eleventh day of a crippling truckers' strike.

State-owned Air France said it continuing to guarantee two-thirds of long-haul flights and a quarter of medium-distance flights during the 48-hour strike, called to protest at deregulation, restructurings and feared job cuts.

Air France Europe, the short-haul unit of Air France, said it was providing fewer than half its normal flights, little changed from Wednesday. It expected that 200 of 480 flights would fly on Thursday.
Striking French truck drivers kept up road blockades slowly strangling the economy for an eleventh day on Thursday after talks with employers broke down during the night over pay demands.
Smaller airlines AOM, TAT and Air Liberte have been virtually unaffected by the strike.
